review_notes: Walked the instruction forward into a list of implied verifiers and the manifest backward against that list: every verifier maps to exactly one ask and there are no orphans. No verifier carries category secondary. One real unfairness found, raised as QC1-2 / D1: answer_prose_floor graded answer.md with (?s)(?:[A-Za-z]+[^A-Za-z]+){60,}, a length-only quantifier with no required content, so a keyword-stuffed stub scored while a genuine explanation went unchecked. Second finding, self-inflicted: the first replacement required the literal strings BR-202, BR-206, AG-307 and 'employee' in answer.md, but submission_format.md never asked for section ids in the prose - so it graded something the instruction did not request. It zeroed all four runs of the stage-3 battery, including two whose checklist_audit.csv and results.json were entirely correct.
change_made: Replaced that pattern with the same sixty-word prose floor plus key-fact set-membership as leading lookaheads - the displacing section (BR-202), both conditionals that decide a verdict (BR-206 and AG-307), and the employment fact they turn on. Chosen over an LLM rubric so grading stays deterministic and judge-free. Then corrected: submission_format.md now asks explicitly for the governing sections the review turns on, in BR-/AG- form, and answer_prose_floor matches the citation form (three or more) rather than named sections or phrasing.
what_to_record: Demonstrated rather than asserted: a 60-word filler stub carrying correct values in the other two deliverables matches the old pattern and fails the new one, scoring 0.0, while gold still scores 1.0 on all ten verifiers. The check matches on cited section values rather than phrasing, so defensible rewordings still pass. After the correction: gold 1.0; a correct audit written in different words, citing three sections and deliberately avoiding the previously required vocabulary, also 1.0; the keyword-stuffed stub still 0.0. So QC1-2 stays closed without rejecting defensible answers.
